connections.why: The blood the Red Cross collected and labelled by the donor's race was the blood of this programme.
Group O blood in a citrate–glucose solution, kept cold and flown to the front, carried Robertson's 1917 depot to a whole theatre of war.
By D-day the Army had a daily airlift to France for blood, penicillin and other biologicals, carrying the drug that the new deep-tank plants had begun to make in quantity that year.
